body:
## Problem

- We have a bunch of ways to "schedule";
    - some not available to Lua;
    - some overlapping and redundant;
    - hard for users to understand the whole picture.
- Possibly could simplify/unify parts.
- Lua has `vim.schedule` but not `vim.schedule_after_typeahead` (name TBD)
    - (TBD: is `SafeState` equivalent to `vim.schedule_after_typeahead` ?)

<details>
<summary>Current surface area:</summary>

| Interface                | Queue                                        | Drains when            | Audience                 |
| ------------------------ | -------------------------------------------- | ---------------------- | ------------------------ |
| `vim.schedule(fn)`       | `loop.events`                                | next event-loop check  | public Lua               |
| `vim.defer_fn(fn, ms)`   | timer                                        | after timeout          | public Lua               |
| `vim.uv.new_*`           | libuv direct                                 | per-handle             | public Lua               |
| `SafeState` autocmd      | autocmd                                      | when nvim becomes idle | public (vimscript & Lua) |
| `loop_schedule_deferred` | `loop.thread_events` → `events` via uv_async | when idle              | C only                   |
| `loop_schedule_fast` (?) | various                                      | depends                | C only                   |

</details>

## Expected behavior

Add a `vim.schedule({ idle = true }, fn)` overload?

- "idle" is the most descriptive but slightly misleading — it's "after input drained," not "user-idle."

Framing:

| name                  | slogan                | wrt to modes           |
|-----------------------| ----------------------| ---------------------- |
| vim.schedule          | async-via-event-queue | *between* mode-dispatches (`K_EVENT` pump), and during blocking pumps (`vim.wait`, RPC waits) |
| vim.schedule_dispatch | async-via-typeahead   | *inside* mode-dispatch (as if user typed it)    |

### Docs: lua.txt

- `vim.schedule(fn)` — run fn off-stack, sometime soon, outside mode.
    - When to use: If you just need a clean point to call an API.
    - Examples: RPC replies, timer callbacks, escaping api-fast contexts, work during `vim.wait`.
    - Internal: the queue is [main_loop.events](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/8e3b216d0b2994b4fa74e0d687c89ff497f42e90/src/nvim/event/loop.h#L12)
- `vim.schedule_dispatch(fn)` — run fn as if the user typed `<Cmd>fn<CR>`.
    - When to use: For anything "potentially interactive", or that transitions modes.
    - Examples: printing messages, prompts, mode transitions (`:startinsert`, `:terminal`, anything that calls `state_enter`).
    - Internal: the "queue" is [typebuf](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/28ffb334cf449c3782ef7e3bf68d150a6cd58227/src/nvim/globals.h#L645)

### Docs: dev-arch.txt

Nvim has two independent queues for "do this later":

1. Event queue (`main_loop.events`). Drained by `state_enter`'s K_EVENT path and by `vim.wait`/    `loop_poll_events`.
    - Producers: vim.schedule, RPC requests, timers, libuv callbacks. Plus `main_loop.fast_events` as a sub-queue that runs even outside `state_enter`.
2. Typeahead (`typebuf`). Drained only by `safe_vgetc` inside `state_enter`'s mode dispatch.
    - Producers: real keystrokes, feedkeys, mappings, `<Cmd>` sequences.

They are *independent*: `vim.wait` won't drain typeahead, and `safe_vgetc` won't run event-queue items (beyond `main_loop.fast_events`).

### Possibly related:

- https://github.com/neovim/neovim/issues/18104
